steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease baking sheets, or line them with parchment paper.

Cream sugar and butter in a large bowl. Beat in sourdough starter and egg. Stir in flour, baking powder, vanilla extract, salt, and baking soda until smooth. Drop dough by teaspoonfuls onto the prepared baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden, 10 to 12 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Sourdough Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These sourdough discard cookies are soft and similar to sugar cookies. The sourdough starter gives them extra tang.
raw_recipe.name: Sweet Sourdough Cookies

review.reviewBody: I used a whole wheat friendship bread starter that I had, and made these cookies vegan. Oil instead of the butter, flax instead of the eggs and I reduced the sugar by 1/4 c since I used a sweet starter. I put in maybe 1/2 c of chips into the batter, but actually like the dough without chocolate in it better. Next time I'd only add some cinnamon to the recipe and keep everything else the same.

These are delicious! They take a lot longer than 10-12 minutes to bake, though - close to 20 minutes for about 3-inch cookies (makes 36-40 cookies). I’ve made these twice, both times adding approximately one cup each of raisins and chopped walnuts. It’s a sticky dough, but I wouldn’t change the amount of any ingredient. This is a handy recipe that helps me avoid discarding sourdough starter. The family likes them.

Great base recipe for sourdough cookies! Read a lot doing chocolate chip add in. Mine is sliced dried apricot topped with apricot jam. Second try- decided to add dried apricot after spooning the dough rather than mixing it in the batter- to distribute them evenly. 
I will explore different add in- candied ginger, dried mango, dried cranberries, dates, and different nuts. 
Great with afternoon tea!

I had good results with a variation on this recipe. I used half and half brown and white sugar, and half and half white and whole wheat flour. I also added cinnamon and chocolate chips. The reviewers who state that this recipe makes a wet dough must be using a very thin starter. I added a quarter cup extra flour and ended up needing more liquid. But the results are delicious and very filling; you can't sit around eating these cookies until they're gone.

Some specific comments: These cookies aren't overly sweet. I like a less sweet cookie, but some people might want to add some more sugar. The consistency is more like mini-cakes than regular cookies. If you have a dense starter, the recommended flour will be more than enough. I found the cooking time to be insufficient. 18 minutes was perfect for my cookies.

I'm definitely making these again, but I'll continue to play around with the recipe.

I enjoyed this recipe. I love using sourdough starter, and what a better place than in cookies!? I used the dough to make both snickerdoodle and chocolate chip type cookies. The reason this didn't get 5 stars was because the dough was too wet and you couldn't do anything with it. Like other reviewers, I added a half cup of additional flour and my cookies were perfectly light and fluffy.

I was so excited to be able to use my sourdough starter instead of wasting it. Cookies texture is amazing and I love that they aren’t overly sweet. I did add the zest of one orange and I made fingerprint cookies using some homemade strawberry orange ginger jelly. I also got 24 good sized cookies from this recipe. Would definitely make again trying different flavors although they are delicious just the way the recipe is written.
A terrific way to use discarded sourdough starter. I added a few drops of orange oil then topped them with a lemon glaze. They are always a hit!

I make sourdough goodies all the time and always looking for new recipes to use my starter. I tweeted this one a bit with using 2 Tablespoons of pure vanilla, using 2 1/4 cups four, 1 cup of milk chocolate chips, 1/2 cup cranberries, 1 cup macadamia nuts. YUMMY!
I agree the cookies are too bland and spread out too much. I added a 1/2 cup more flour and 1 tsp of chai spice. Of course you need 1 cup chocolate chips (or dried blueberries). Good initial recipe.

Decent base recipe that is fun to play with! 
I added 3/4 cup sugar, added cinnamon and nutmeg, and then topped them with a cinnamon sugar spice blend. Mine turned out very puffy and light almost like a little muffin top cookie. I will probably use this as a base recipe for many cookie variations since it’s a great quick way to use up sourdough discard!!

I use the Amish Friendship Starter for this recipe. However, I make them into Snickerdoodles by topping the cookies with a mixture of 2 tablespoons of cinnamon to 1/2 cup sugar before baking. Yum!!!!!!! Adding an extra 1/4 cup of flour to the recipe mixture makes the cookies maintain their shape while baking.

made this recipe but added some almond extract on top of the vanilla extract, as well as some cardamom, allspice, and cinnamon. i also added chocolate chips and some almond granola. the end result was still somewhat bland, but had a good texture and was very pillowy. if i made this again, i might try to add fruit/zest instead.
Excellent! Very soft and cake-like. I baked them for exactly 10 minutes. I made the recipe as written. Has a nice sourdough flavor that's not overwhelming.

Used 3/4 cup sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar and 3/4 cup choco chips. Dough needed more liquid and we decided to add tonic water instead of tap water. We did not have milk available. Baked for 15 min on parchment. Bottoms came out great. Cookie was different than a regular cookie. Not as sweet, but soooo good!

Very simple to make. I only used 1/2 cup of sourdough discard, it was all I had and initially I read it wrong and used 1 tsp of baking soda the first time I made them. I like it that way, it’s fluffier and goes good with coffee and tea. This recipes a keeper!
These were easy to make-I thought they were just okay. I wanted to find a recipe to use for my discarded sourdough starter. They were worth making one time. Thank you for the recipe!! :)

I used 3/4 cup white sugar and 1/4 cup brown sugar and I also added chocolate chips. I think they are tasty. As others have said, it's a nice basic recipe that you can play around with. Mine were baked in 12 minutes.

I used this recipe for my very first use of my very first sourdough starter. I also needed a chocolate fix, so I swapped 1/4 cup of flour for dark unsweetened cocoa powder, and sprinkled them with sea salt. I love them!! They're like little mini chocolate cakes! Moist and light. This recipe will be fun to use as a base for other creative sourdough cookies! Thank you for sharing it!

Very light and airy. Not too sweet even with Heath Bits and chocolate chips. I used half white and brown sugar and half Gluten free flax & Ancient grains and white flour. I also included pecans. I will experiment more with this recipe.
After looking at the reviews I added butterscotch chips. They were good but a little dry. I'm not a great baker.
